b2-diaszpora-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Why People Left for America
b2-diaszpora-01.scenario: In a village in Szabolcs county, a young visitor asks you why so many people left for America around 1900 and what became of them.
b2-diaszpora-01.prompt: Tell the visitor why many people emigrated, where they worked, and what some did when they came back.
cues: Say where they worked in America
Say what some of the returnees built at home
b2-diaszpora-01.target: Sokan kivándoroltak a tengerentúlra, mert kevés volt a föld és alacsonyak voltak a bérek. A szénbányákban és a gyárakban dolgoztak. Közülük egyesek hazatértek, és téglaházat építettek.
b2-diaszpora-01.english: Many people emigrated overseas because there was little land and wages were low. They worked in the coal mines and the factories. Some of them came home and built a brick house.
b2-diaszpora-01.canDo: I can explain the historical causes and demographic patterns of the turn-of-the-century Hungarian migration to the Americas.

b2-diaszpora-02.title: Communicative Challenge: After 1956
b2-diaszpora-02.scenario: At the Hungarian House in Toronto, a young listener asks you what happened in November 1956 and how the refugees managed in the West.
b2-diaszpora-02.prompt: Tell the listener how many people left in 1956 and how many of them settled in.
cues: Say roughly how many people left the country
Say that many of them settled into the new countries
b2-diaszpora-02.target: 1956 novemberében körülbelül kétszázezer ember hagyta el az országot. Sokan viszonylag gyorsan beilleszkedtek az új országokban, és újrakezdték az életüket.
b2-diaszpora-02.english: In November 1956 about two hundred thousand people left the country. Many of them settled into the new countries fairly quickly and started their lives anew.
b2-diaszpora-02.canDo: I can describe the 1956 Hungarian refugee wave and the international response to 200,000 asylum seekers.

b2-diaszpora-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Keeping the Language Alive
b2-diaszpora-03.scenario: At the Hungarian House in Cleveland, a parent asks you how the community keeps Hungarian alive for the children.
b2-diaszpora-03.prompt: Tell the parent which institutions hand the language on and what the Hungarian House does for the community.
cues: Say which institutions hand down the mother tongue
Say what the Hungarian House does for the community
b2-diaszpora-03.target: A hétvégi iskolák és a cserkészet révén átörökítették az anyanyelvet a következő nemzedékre. A Magyar Ház összetartotta a közösséget.
b2-diaszpora-03.english: Through the weekend schools and scouting they handed the mother tongue down to the next generation. The Hungarian House held the community together.
b2-diaszpora-03.canDo: I can analyze the institutional infrastructure of the Hungarian diaspora: scouting, weekend schools, and cultural houses.

b2-diaszpora-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Working in Austria and London
b2-diaszpora-04.scenario: In Sopron, a friend asks you what the 2004 EU accession meant for people who want to work abroad.
b2-diaszpora-04.prompt: Tell your friend what many people did after 2004 and where they found work.
cues: Say that many people commute to Austria and keep their home here
Say that many people found a job in London
b2-diaszpora-04.target: Sopron környékéről tízezrek ingáznak Ausztriába, és megtartják magyarországi lakóhelyüket. Sokan Londonban helyezkednek el.
b2-diaszpora-04.english: Tens of thousands from the Sopron area commute to Austria and keep their homes in Hungary. Many find employment in London.
b2-diaszpora-04.canDo: I can discuss the European Union freedom of movement and its demographic consequences for Hungary after 2004.

b2-diaszpora-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Coming Home
b2-diaszpora-05.scenario: In Budapest, a friend who has just moved back from London asks you why people come home and what to expect.
b2-diaszpora-05.prompt: Tell your friend why many people return and what they have to get used to again.
cues: Say what they have to get used to again
b2-diaszpora-05.target: A hazatérők közül sokan a nagyszülők és a barátok közelsége miatt döntenek így. Újra hozzá kell szokniuk az itthoni ügyintézéshez.
b2-diaszpora-05.english: Many of the returnees decide so because their grandparents and friends are close. They have to get used to the administration at home again.
b2-diaszpora-05.canDo: I can analyze current trends in return migration and the reintegration challenges faced by returning Hungarians.

b2-diaszpora-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Century of Leaving
b2-diaszpora-consolidation.scenario: At an émigré conference in Toronto, a guest asks you to sum up Hungarian emigration since 1890.
b2-diaszpora-consolidation.prompt: Sum up the three great waves and say what is happening today.
cues: Say what happened after 2004 and what many do today
b2-diaszpora-consolidation.target: A századfordulón sokan kivándoroltak a tengerentúlra, 1956 után körülbelül kétszázezren menekültek Nyugatra, 2004 után pedig százezrek mentek Nyugat-Európába dolgozni. Ma sokan hazatelepülnek.
b2-diaszpora-consolidation.english: Around 1900 many people emigrated overseas, after 1956 about two hundred thousand fled to the West, and after 2004 hundreds of thousands went to Western Europe to work. Today many move back home.
b2-diaszpora-consolidation.canDo: I can synthesize the historical trajectories of Hungarian emigration from 1890 to the present day.
